notes: every case is signed once through the patched c2pa-rs (extended patch build) and validated twice: p1 = the patch as in the paper (ML-DSA signing and COSE verification only), p2 = p1 plus ML-DSA in certificate path validation (cert_signing_alg, signing_alg_to_sig_and_hash_oid, validator_for_sig_and_hash_algs)
PKI: root -> intermediate -> leaf per algorithm, generated for the run; leaf EKU c2pa-kp-claimSigning; the root is not placed in x5chain unless the case says so

time-stamping authority and its trust anchor are ES256 for every algorithm; OCSP responses come in both RFC 6960 forms: signed by the issuing intermediate (CA-signed, no certificates in the response) and signed by a delegated responder (id-kp-OCSPSigning, issued by the same intermediate, certificate in the response)

x5t, no-credential, algorithm-mismatch and the *_direct cases are built by the harness (direct COSE handling, no time stamp) because the library's signer never emits them: c2pa-rs refuses at signing time to sign with a leaf that fails its certificate profile (wrong EKU, no digitalSignature); chain_noroot_direct is the control showing a harness-built COSE of a good chain validates
crypto_valid: claimSignature.validated reported and no claimSignature failure; profile_compliant: no signingCredential.invalid/expired or algorithm.unsupported; trusted: validation_state Trusted

trust policy: the EKU list c2pa-rs ships as default (emailProtection, documentSigning, timeStamping, OCSPSigning, MS C2PA signing, c2pa-kp-claimSigning) on the manifest anchor set, timeStamping on the TSA anchor set; eku_timestamping is also validated under a claimSigning-only policy
verify_ms is the Reader call inside the harness; max_rss_bytes is the whole process
short-lived leaves expire 300 s after generation and are validated after expiry
expected outcomes follow the C2PA 2.5 text (October 2026); where the first draft of the runner expected otherwise, spec_basis gives the clause that decides the case
